analysis:
All three changes are test and CI-test scaffolding. None touches provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, key custody, cache crypto or fan helper code.

1. Gemma4StagePagedSyntheticTests.swift line 21 adds a `.boundedBufferCache` suite trait. QwenTensorParallelPrefixDepthTests.swift line 13 adds `.boundedBufferCache(gib: 4)`. Both only bound the MLX buffer cache during tests. The trait is defined elsewhere and is not visible here. Test bodies are otherwise unchanged, and no production KV or prefix-cache behavior (T-041, TB-007) is altered. The depth test uses in-memory QwenTensorParallelBatchPrefixCache instances. It does not exercise the SSD tier's at-rest artifacts, HMAC names or TTL.

2. scripts/test-cluster-test-plan.py (head lines ~301-307) changes an offline unit-test assertion. GPU shards of test-cluster-gpu are now expected to take `runs-on` from `fromJSON(inputs.routes)[format('<job>-<shard>', matrix.shard)]`. The assertion also requires per-shard route entries `<job>-<shard> macos_arm64` in the route job. Previously the expectation was a fixed BLACKSMITH_MAC runner with no route entries. This tracks a CI workflow change that is not in the supplied evidence. The CI runner-routing and runner-trust implications, such as which runner pool the non-blocking GPU tests land on or whether `inputs.routes` is attacker-influenced, cannot be assessed from this diff. The real workflow YAML and the route job were not supplied, so that is an unverified contract. It is CI infrastructure, which is outside the retained provider threat-model scope, and no concrete regression is evidenced.

No threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations are affected by these diffs. The next pass should check the workflow/route changes that this test asserts, since only the test side was supplied.
